Jonesboro by the numbers

How big is Jonesboro and why does the city matter for property tax?

Jonesboro is the fifth-largest city in Arkansas and the second largest by land area, behind Little Rock. The Census Bureau counted 78,576 residents in 2020 and put the 2025 estimate at 83,296, and the city covers about 80.7 square miles at an elevation of 276 feet.

It sits on Crowley's Ridge in northeast Arkansas and is the western county seat of Craighead County. The city's own growth plan, called Destination 100K, aims at passing 100,000 residents, according to Mayor Harold Copenhaver in a July 2025 report.

The city's early years shaped its center. The Cotton Belt railroad laid track north of downtown in 1881, the first courthouse burned in 1869 and later ones burned in 1876 and 1878, and the present courthouse was finished in 1934. Hattie Caraway, widow of Jonesboro resident Thaddeus Caraway, became the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate in 1932.

What drives the Jonesboro economy?

Arkansas State University is the largest employer, directly or indirectly, with St. Bernards and NEA Baptist anchoring healthcare. Agriculture, government work, retail and manufacturing fill out the picture.

Food processing has deep roots here. Riceland Foods built what was then the world's largest rice mill in 1930, and City Water and Light, formed as a municipal utility in 1906, is credited with helping attract industry through low rates.

The Jonesboro metro had 65,608 people employed in April 2025, up 1.8 percent from a year earlier. A.State recently broke ground on the state's first public veterinary school, and the NYIT College of Osteopathic Medicine runs a campus there.

Which offices tax a Jonesboro house?

The city does not collect the property tax bill. Craighead County does, and the same bill includes the city, school district and other levies for the parcel.

  • Craighead County Assessor, Hannah Towell, 511 S. Union St., Suite 130, 870-933-4572, sets the appraised value.
  • Craighead County Tax Collector, Wes Eddington, 511 Union Street, Suite 107, 870-933-4560, bills and collects.
  • City of Jonesboro Planning & Zoning, 300 S. Church Street, 870-932-0406, handles zoning and permits.

The county explains that taxable value is 20 percent of the appraised value, multiplied by the millage for where the property sits. The county's collector page says taxes can be paid from the first business day of March through October 15 of the following year, with a 10 percent penalty after that date. We did not find a current Jonesboro millage figure on an opened official page, so check your bill.

Which school district is my Jonesboro house in?

Six public school districts operate within Jonesboro city limits: Jonesboro, Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay and Brookland. A single city address does not fix the school district, and the district's millage is part of the bill.

The 2020 Census put the median age in Craighead County at 33.5, with 66.3 percent of residents living in urban areas.

The Jonesboro School District was set up in 1899 and runs Jonesboro High School. Its elementary schools became magnet schools in the 2007 to 2008 school year. A buyer will ask which district serves the house, so know it before the first showing.

Arkansas State University dates to the First District Agricultural School, which held its first classes on October 3, 1910, and the Northeast Arkansas Career and Tech Center is also in the city.

What weather and land conditions affect Jonesboro homes?

Jonesboro has a humid subtropical climate, with average annual precipitation of 52.02 inches and 3.9 inches of snow. Summer highs average 89.7 degrees in July, and January lows average 26.7 degrees.

Tornadoes are part of the city's history. An F4 tornado struck on May 15 and 16, 1968, destroying 164 homes and killing at least 34 people. Another F4 hit on May 27, 1973, killing three and injuring 289. An EF3 tornado on March 28, 2020, severely damaged The Mall at Turtle Creek.

The ridge helped the town grow. The elevation of Crowley's Ridge kept Jonesboro out of periodic floods, which mattered to early development, while the New Madrid earthquakes of 1811 and 1812 created the "sunken lands" near the city.

  • Keep records of roof and storm-damage repairs.
  • Note whether a storm shelter or safe room exists.
  • Check the age of heating and cooling equipment, since the climate has both hot summers and cold snaps.

Which Jonesboro rules might apply before I sell?

The city Planning & Zoning Department handles zoning, rezoning, conditional use and variance requests, and its permit list includes a home occupation permit and a short term rental application. Online permit applications are available for residential, commercial and sign work.

Resources on the city page include the 2018 Land Use Plan, the Master Street Plan and a Duplex Ordinance. Zoning lookups, setbacks, accessory structures and guesthouse questions appear in its FAQs, and the full city code is on Municode. The Board of Zoning Adjustment and the Metropolitan Area Planning Commission publish meeting schedules.

The city page does not state specific short term rental rules, so we are not describing them here. If a house has a garage conversion, a second dwelling or an unpermitted addition, ask the department before listing.

How do roads and transit shape a Jonesboro sale?

Several highways meet in Jonesboro: AR 1, AR 18, US 49, US 63, US 78 and Interstate 555. Jonesboro Municipal Airport has commercial service through the federal Essential Air Service program with Southern Airways Express.

GOJO, Jonesboro Economical Transit, operates four fixed routes and paratransit, and Greyhound provides intercity bus service. Freight rail lines include the old Cotton Belt, Frisco and Missouri Pacific routes.

Distance to a rail line or the interstate is something a buyer can check in minutes, so describe your block accurately in the listing materials.

How does a Jonesboro sale close with taxes owed?

A Jonesboro sale closes with the title company paying unpaid property tax from the proceeds and recording the deed with the Craighead County Circuit Clerk. The state's real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration, which comes to $660 on a $200,000 price.

If taxes stay unpaid, the parcel can be certified for a tax-delinquent land auction run by the Commissioner of State Lands. A regional auction was held in Jonesboro in August 2025 at 2840 S. Caraway Road, with redemption allowed until 4 p.m. on the last business day before the sale. Auction sales are final under Act 241.

The Craighead County Assessor handles questions about value. Appeals go to the County Board of Equalization, and the state says the last day to schedule a hearing is the third Monday in August.

More questions about Jonesboro, AR Property Tax Guide

Who sends the Jonesboro property tax bill?

Craighead County does. The County Tax Collector, Wes Eddington, bills and collects, and the County Assessor sets the value.

Does Jonesboro have its own property tax rate?

The bill combines city, school district and other levies for your parcel. We could not confirm a current Jonesboro rate on an opened official page, so check the bill or ask the Collector.

How many school districts serve Jonesboro?

Six: Jonesboro, Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay and Brookland.

Where do I get a Jonesboro building or zoning permit?

From City of Jonesboro Planning & Zoning at 300 S. Church Street, phone 870-932-0406. Online permit applications are also available.

Can I sell a Jonesboro house with a tax lien or unpaid taxes?

Yes. Title companies pay unpaid property tax from the sale proceeds at closing. Settle the balance before any state auction date, because auction sales are final.

What tornadoes have hit Jonesboro?

F4 tornadoes struck on May 15 and 16, 1968, and May 27, 1973, and an EF3 hit on March 28, 2020.
